title: PREDICT - Prehospital triage for suspected acute coronary syndrome without ST-segment elevation
summary:
PREDICT is a research project that aims to improve the care of people who experience chest pain and may be suspected of having a heart attack. 
Today, many such patients are transported to emergency departments even though most ultimately do not have a heart attack. This puts a significant burden on emergency services. PREDICT seeks to evaluate whether using a rapid point-of-care troponin test directly in the emergency vehicle, together with a digital decision support tool (“ACS-Pathfinder”), may help to identify heart attacks earlier and reduce unnecessary hospital transports.
The calibration study investigates how often patients treated by emergency medical services for suspected heart attack truly have a myocardial infarction. Understanding this frequency is essential for adjusting the algorithm so that it functions reliably in real-world prehospital settings.
Approximately 300 patients will be enrolled during routine emergency missions. Their medical care will remain unchanged. In addition, a point-of-care troponin test will be performed using either venous blood, and the result will be documented in the ACS-Pathfinder application, which will not display any decision or risk estimate in this phase. After hospital treatment, the final diagnosis will be collected to determine whether a heart attack was confirmed. These data will allow the algorithm to be calibrated for use in prehospital setting.
conditions: Suspected acute myocardial infarction (AMI) within the spectrum of acute coronary syndrome without ST-segment elevation (NSTE-ACS).  The study focuses on improving early, prehospital diagnosis and triage of these patients using a high-sensitivity troponin point-of-care test and a digital decision algorithm (ACS-Pathfinder).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Suspected myocardial infarction
• Symptom onset >30 minutes before arrival of emergency medical services
• Written consent
Exclusion criteria:
• STEMI detected on initial ECG
• Suspected NSTE-ACS with hemodynamic instability, life-threatening arrhythmias, or cardiac arrest
• Non-ischemic causes requiring mandatory hospitalization
• Emergency physician dispatch at the request of a primary care physician
• Age <18 Jahre
